symptom: `describe demo user` of a demo user with no user roles printed `create or modify demo user 'u' password '***';`, which does not parse (the clause form required at least one role in `( … )`), so describe → exec of such a project failed at that statement
cause: The clause-form grammar `password 'p' [entity E] (Role, …)` had no way to say "no roles"; the emitter simply left the list out. A positional clause list with a mandatory tail cannot express an empty value, the same shape #707 found in the user role's positional module-role list
insight: Fixed as a side effect of phase 3.6 (ako/mxcli#755): the header became a ( Password: …, Entity: …, UserRoles: (…) ) list in which UserRoles may be empty or omitted, and describe writes it. When a describe emitter conditionally omits a clause, check the grammar accepts the statement without it — `TestDescribeDemoUserWritesThePropertyList` parses the output for the no-roles case. Positional headers with required tails are the recurring source of these non-reparses; converting them to property lists removes the class
